title: You Were Saying Words...
text:
You were saying words

intimate, silent.


Words that are spoken

from love to love,

from one mouth to another mouth.


The secret poem

was made for everyone,

the small words

memorable, blessed.


The daily feats,

illusions of the day,

the smallest things;

shared words,

useful, generous.


The secret poem

was made for everyone,

the small words

—others I shall not say—

will last like rocks.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the small shared words as the durable substance of the poem.

title: Turned Back upon Itself
text:
Turned back upon itself, the human gaze

is, alas, only a sad bewilderment.

We know nothing, we shall never know,

in present pain or in the blind future

there is only something that is certain, certain, certain:

dreams have lost the battle.


That the smallest longings, as much

as the principal hopes,

have systematically been ruined.

On the horizon that remains equally for us are missing

the small rose and the great sun.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the repeated certainty and the final absent rose and sun.

title: To Write
text:
To write you went day by day

beside the murmur, beside the continuous sea.

Promontories of shadow could not

disorient you or silence your voice.


Thus the powerful feelings

were justified, the actions,

discourses, the inextinguishable passion

will not die... You will live with them.


You will place in the matter of your craft

this final life, breath and meaning.

Human faith among the inert word,

human light in the immortal waiting.




1966
editorial_note: The translation keeps writing as craft, breath, and human light inside inert words.

title: The Birds Came
text:
The birds came and disappeared.

Words return to their remote dream.

Who speaks of hope? I feel cold.


Over pain and still more in joy,

—over these roses and in the rivers—

before as after over life.

In love,

at the beginning, at the end of delirium.


The fruit of the trees ceased.

In the human womb fruit abounds.

The mountain rises, collapses.

Without meaning the earth turns, turns.

The shadow remains so deep.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's cold motion from birds and words into the turning earth.

title: She Wanted to Follow You
text:
She wanted to follow you, shut inside her dream

she scratched at the doors so that you would hear her,

so that you would answer she called you with screams.


Her defeated word sat down gravely

as if a deep thought occupied her,

and among her own blood she went weaving shadows,

in her faith, in her harmony, in her human substance.


We confused, she toward you, without course...

In the midst of two worlds totally disoriented.


Her pulse beats here, her memory in your nothing.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the woman suspended between two worlds and ending in another's nothing.

We confused, she toward you, without course. ..

In the midst of two worlds totally disoriented.


Her pulse beats here, her memory in your nothing.
editorial_note: This related version preserves the source's unusual spaced ellipsis before the final disorientation.

title: My Father Has Died...
text:
My father has died.

His absence repeats itself each day

in the empty home.

I ask,

and besides absence and besides

losing the roads of this earth,

what is death?


I ask you, father, what is death?

Have you found the peace you deserved?

Did you find shelter in a new house

or do you wander, and suffer beneath the cold

of the greatest winter, of total

lovelessness?


I ask you, father, if the dead are something,

or if death is only

an immense word that contains

everything that does not exist.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the direct filial questions and the final definition of death as an immense word.

title: I Do Not Know Where They Come From...
text:
I do not know where they come from,

your laughter, your joy,

in what instant you learned

to look face to face

at everything we fear.

To look it in the eyes

as if there were nothing

to fear

and your gaze

had discovered

among so much disorder

a principle of light.


As if you were

at the edge of mystery

and nothing surprised

your faith

and you spoke to us

not of what you are seeing,

but of what you feel

coming

and understand so easily...


Thus then you separate

from terror its daily

wrapping

and your hand

traces in the darkness

a safe path.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the speaker's wonder at a gaze that extracts light from disorder.

title: The Neighborhood of the Sea Is Abolished
text:
The neighborhood of the sea is abolished:

It is enough to know it guards our backs,

That there is an immense green window

Through which to throw oneself swimming.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Reyes's compact image of the sea as a guarded green window.

title: Barely
text:
Sometimes, made of nothing,

an effluvium rises from the ground.

Suddenly, quietly,

the cedar sighs with aroma.


Since we are the thin

dissolution of a secret,

as soon as the soul yields a little

the fountain of a dream overflows.


Miserable thing, vague

reason, when, in the silence,

a kind of sun-glare

descends upon me from your memory!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the delicate movement from scent and secrecy to remembered light.
